tools.name: search_offers
tools.description: Search current startup credits and deals, including cloud credits, SaaS discounts, free tiers, grants, perks, and partner offers. Filter by query, vendor, or category and evaluate eligibility from typed company facts; unknowns remain explicit.

tools.name: compare_offers
tools.description: Compare two to ten startup credit or deal offers side by side, including value, access requirements, eligibility, freshness, and evidence. Unknown eligibility and unsupported stacking remain explicit.

tools.name: inspect_evidence
tools.description: Inspect the provenance behind startup credits and deals. Resolve one to ten exact revisions to supporting events and observations, including freshness and dispute status.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Track added, changed, withdrawn, and removed startup credits, discounts, free tiers, perks, and deals through Sourcey's signed change feed after an optional cursor.

tools.name: search_readiness
tools.description: Search published Agent Readiness report cards. Each card says whether an agent can do one named job on a vendor's service through its machine interfaces: the Operate letter (A+ to F, or a dash when not yet rated) over Discover, Delegation, Pay, Job, Confirm and Sustain, where a person has to step in

tools.name: get_readiness
tools.description: Get one published Agent Readiness report card: the job and the interface it ran on, the Operate letter and its statement, each step's outcome, approvals and human workarounds, the Onboard level, the evidence label, discovery facts from the service's own descriptors, the declared surface, policy iden

tools.name: prepare_declaration
tools.description: Prepare the canonical Agent Readiness declaration for one service and job: participants, endpoints, API and MCP interfaces, delegated authority, payment, recovery and library-job bindings. The company must already exist in Sourcey and resolves by exact identity; an unknown company returns identity_a

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: Discover Sourcey's enabled paid agent services and canonical HTTP resources, including exact request and response contracts, price floor, policy links, and x402 discovery. Payment and durable job status remain on the product HTTP API; this read-only MCP tool never signs, settles, or interprets a pay

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_changes, search_readiness, get_readiness · Public sink: prepare_declaration.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_changes, search_readiness, get_readiness · Public sink: prepare_declaration

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "prepare_declaration" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Prepare canonical GitHub-ready YAML for an independent Agent Readiness assessment of one vendor product, API, SaaS service, authentication path, payment path, provisioning flow, operating interface, recovery flow, and exact agent standard. Resolves only exact Sourcey Entity identity, never assigns a" → after: "Prepare the canonical Agent Readiness declaration for one service and job: participants, endpoints, API and MCP interfaces, delegated authority, payment, recovery and library-job bindings. The company must already exist in Sourcey and resolves by exact identity; an unknown company returns identity_a"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
